chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Aqabah, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Satan cried out four cries: the first was on the day he was cursed, and when he was sent down to the Earth, and when Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was appointed at the time of the Prophets, and when the Mother of the Book was revealed. And he roared two roars: when Adam ate from the tree, and when he was sent down from Paradise.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: The Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What were the four cries and two roars of Satan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies four distinct cries and two roars of Iblis, linking his spiritual degradation to pivotal moments in cosmic history, including the appointment of Prophet Muhammad during the *fatrah* (period of intermission) and the revelation of *Umm al-Kitab*. This narration underscores the continuity of divine guidance and the cosmic significance of the Prophet's mission in Shia eschatology. The events highlight the transition from Adam's fall to the ultimate restoration of authority through the Prophet and the Quran.
